title: Cech sections agree over one connected geometric fibre
statement: Let f:T\to S be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], let \Omega be an algebraically closed field and q:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Assume U=T\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. For a sheaf F of sets on S_{et} [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] and a global section a of f^{-1}F, set D=T\times_S T, g=\operatorname{pr}_1\circ f and E=D\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega [def-pc-fibre-product]. The two Cech pullbacks of a, identified as sections of g^{-1}F by the unit-compatible composition comparisons and the pullback-condition equality [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], have equal inverse-image restrictions along E\to D. Restrictions use the adjunction unit and the canonical terminal-object pullback lift. Only U is assumed connected; no global compatibility on D is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0A3H (lemma-sections-upstairs), final paragraph, compatibility before fpqc descent; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A3H

proof.text: Put p:U -> T and h:U -> Spec Omega. Pull a back by the inverse-image unit along p. The unit-compatible composition comparisons and p followed by f = h followed by q identify its terminal section with a section of (h followed by q)^-1 F. Since U is connected, the bijective constant-section map gives a unique e in F_q representing this section.

The two maps E -> U are the pullback lifts pairing d followed by pr_i with the common projection v:E -> Spec Omega. Their composites with h are v. Pullback uniqueness identifies E with U times_(Spec Omega) U. Naturality of inverse-image units moves the terminal lifts through the two restrictions. Associativity of the chosen inverse-image composition comparisons identifies each restricted Cech section with the corresponding pullback of the section in the preceding step; the maps of terminal pullbacks agree because both their projections agree.

The naturality clause of the geometric-fibre constant-section theorem identifies both pullbacks with the constant section of e on E. Its comparison is an isomorphism, so transport back gives the claimed equality. No connectedness or nonemptiness of E is needed; nonempty connected U is the sole connectedness assumption.

mathlib_searches.query: Pullbacks of a section along both Cech projections agree after restriction to a connected geometric fibre
A global section of an inverse image etale sheaf has equal restrictions along two maps over the base if geometric fibres are connected
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits, all Scheme.Hom.appLE or Scheme.congr_app identities; none compares Cech sections on a connected geometric fibre.

mathlib_searches.results: No Mathlib statement for this fibre-local Cech equality. Existing EtaleGeometricFibreConstantSections provides the constant sections and their naturality, but not their identification with the two restricted Cech sections. Existing EtaleConnectedFibresSectionCompatible is the global theorem, not the local statement.

theorem etaleSet_cech_sections_agree_on_connected_geometric_fibre
    {S T : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S)
    (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (q : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S)
    [ConnectedSpace (pullback f q : Scheme.{u})]
    (F : Sheaf S.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)))
    (a : ((L f).obj F).obj.obj (op I[T])) :
    let D := pullback f f
    let g := pullback.fst f f ≫ f
    let E := pullback g q
    let d := pullback.fst g q
    let G := (L g).obj F
    R[D,E,d,G]
      (((Classical.choose etaleSetInverseImageCompositionUnits.2.2
          S T (pullback f f) f (pullback.fst f f)).hom.app F).hom.app
        (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 (pullback f f))))
        (((Scheme.etaleSetPullback (pullback.fst f f)).obj
            ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback f).obj F)).obj.map
          (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk
            (pullback.lift (pullback.fst f f) (𝟙 (pullback f f))
              ((Category.comp_id _).trans (Category.id_comp _).symm))
            (by simp) :
            Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 (pullback f f)) ⟶
              (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ (pullback.fst f f)).obj
                (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 T))).op
          (((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
            (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ (pullback.fst f f)) _
            (T.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
            ((pullback f f).smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)).unit.app
              ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback f).obj F)).hom.app
            (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 T))) a))) =
    R[D,E,d,G]
      (Eq.mp (congrArg (fun k : pullback f f ⟶ S ↦
          ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback k).obj F).obj.obj
            (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 (pullback f f)))))
          (pullback.condition (f := f) (g := f)).symm)
        (((Classical.choose etaleSetInverseImageCompositionUnits.2.2
            S T (pullback f f) f (pullback.snd f f)).hom.app F).hom.app
          (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 (pullback f f))))
          (((Scheme.etaleSetPullback (pullback.snd f f)).obj
              ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback f).obj F)).obj.map
            (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk
              (pullback.lift (pullback.snd f f) (𝟙 (pullback f f))
                ((Category.comp_id _).trans (Category.id_comp _).symm))
              (by simp) :
              Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 (pullback f f)) ⟶
                (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ (pullback.snd f f)).obj
                  (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 T))).op
            (((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
              (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ (pullback.snd f f)) _
              (T.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
              ((pullback f f).smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)).unit.app
                ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback f).obj F)).hom.app
              (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 T))) a))))
